html:
A private political alliance formed around 60 BCE by three leading Romans: Julius Caesar, Pompey and Marcus Crassus. "Triumvirate" means rule of three men, though this one had no legal standing.

Each had been blocked by the Senate, led by Cato the Younger. Pompey wanted land for his veterans and his settlement of the east confirmed. Crassus wanted relief for the tax-farming companies he backed. Caesar wanted the consulship. Together they controlled votes, money and soldiers. As consul in 59 BCE Caesar forced their measures through and won a five-year command that became the Gallic Wars. Pompey married Caesar's daughter Julia. Cicero was asked to join and refused.

The three renewed the deal at Luca in 56 BCE. Pompey and Crassus became consuls again in 55 BCE and Caesar's command was extended. Then it came apart. Julia died in 54 BCE, and Crassus was killed by the Parthians at the Battle of Carrhae in 53 BCE. Pompey and Caesar became rivals, and the rivalry led to Caesar's civil war. A legal version, the Second Triumvirate, followed in 43 BCE.
sum: A private political alliance formed around 60 BCE by three leading Romans: Julius Caesar, Pompey and Marcus Crassus. "Triumvirate" means rule of three men, though this one had no legal standing.
